There sure is.. A tin whistle is end blown like a recorder. Here is a great example of a whistle player doing whistle things. A flute is side blown, like a beer bottle. All whistles are simple system, meaning no mechanical keys and they are all diatonic. Each one plays in a single key, so you have to have several whistles. Flutes can be simple system or have mechanical keys that make them chromatic. I have two left, one is a simple system Casey Burns Irish flute in the key of D, and a silver Boehm system chromatic flute that I play whenever I'm not in D/Bm, which is 99% of the time. Here is Sir James Galway, widely recognized as the best flute player in the world.
